title: Matthew Morrison is back on Broadway for the first time in over a dec...
transcript: I just saw Matthew Morrison's first performance as Bobby Darin in just in time on Broadway. And this is going to be my full breakdown, all of my thoughts on Matthew, as well as how I think the show works without Jonathan Groff. I actually thought he was really excellent. And if you don't know, the actor who plays Bobby Darin begins the show as themselves. And so when Jonathan began the show, he talked a lot about his relationship with Bobby Darin and the things that they had in common. But Matthew's early dialogue is all focused on how this is his big Broadway return after 10 years, and how one of his first Broadway credits was in the ensemble of Rocky Horror in that same theatre. And now here he is, 26 years later as a leading man. It's a very full circle moment, and you could tell that it means a lot to him. There is, sadly, no references to his work in Hairspray or on Glee, which I, and I imagine the multiple people I saw dressed up as Sue Sylvester were very disappointed about. But I do think it sets up the evening very nicely. And it's hard to imagine a more perfect role for his big Broadway return because this role is so in his wheelhouse. He gets to show off his singing, his acting, his dancing especially. I think he really nails the drive of Bobby Darin. His Bobby has a real intensity. About him. And I felt the weight of that ticking clock so much more with Matthew's performance than I did with Jonathan's. And while it is admittedly hard to not compare him to Jonathan Groff, the fact that this show lets the actor playing Bobby Darin bring so much of themselves to this role, it never feels like a replica of Jonathan's performance. And because of that, I do believe that the show can work without Jonathan Groff. Because all you really need to be a good Bobby Darin is you need to be a showman. And Matthew Morrison is a showman. And seeing him in the show felt really special, not just because it's his big return to Broadway after 10 years, but also because he's only doing 23 shows. It's an extremely limited run. So these themes of these moments that we share together being so fleeting, they really ring true because it feels like something that's only gonna happen a handful of times, and then it's over. And I think there's something really beautiful about that.
